mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate rise above 0.5% in 3 months signals tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in payroll employment signals strong labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE down and PAYEMS up) fails to produce positive returns in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: In housing recovery regime (HOUST > 600k units), rising residential sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In HOUST > 600 periods, RSAFS rising fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 100 indicates robust manufacturing output that supports corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 100 (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 550k units signals weak consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when HOUST < 550 (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8.0%), a decline in unemployment rate signals improving labor conditions that boost consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In UNRATE > 8.0 periods, unemployment decline fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate rise and CPIAUCSL decline below 1.5% signals tightening with disinflation, reducing real rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL falling) fails to produce negative returns in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).
